jobs_results.description:
Geom is building an AI platform focused on production-scale architecture, helping homebuilders automate repetitive drafting, review, and construction-document workflows. Its technology integrates with the tools and plan sets builders already use, reducing manual effort and improving consistency. Backed by prominent technology investors, Geoms team combines deep expertise in architecture, homebuilding, AI, and startup environments. The company is headquartered in San Francisco and operates at the intersection of built environment and advanced machine learning. Additional information about Geom and its platform can be .

The Role

Were looking for a Computer Vision / Machine Learning Engineer to help build the intelligence behind Geom.

Youll work on challenging problems at the intersection of computer vision, multimodal AI, geometry, machine learning, and architectural data. The goal is not simply to recognize what appears in a drawing, but to understand the elements, relationships, constraints, and intent represented within complex architectural plan sets, and turn that understanding into reliable automation.

This is an early-stage role with the opportunity to make an impact. Youll work closely with our engineering, product, and architecture teams to take ideas from experimentation through production and apply them to real-world building plans at scale.

What Youll Work On



Develop models and systems for understanding architectural drawings, floor plans, construction documents, and other complex visual information.Build computer vision and multimodal pipelines for detecting, classifying, extracting, and reasoning about architectural elements and their relationships.Combine vision models, foundation models, geometric reasoning, and structured representations to create semantic understanding of plan sets.Develop methods for matching and tracking elements across drawings, sheets, revisions, and plan variations.Work on problems involving object detection, segmentation, document understanding, spatial reasoning, image registration, vector geometry, and visual similarity.Design training, evaluation, and data-generation pipelines that allow models to improve rapidly as we encounter new plan types and workflows.Develop practical approaches for working with imperfect, noisy, inconsistent, and highly variable real-world architectural data.Translate experimental ML capabilities into reliable production systems.Establish evaluation frameworks and metrics for model accuracy, reliability, and downstream automation quality.Collaborate directly with domain experts to understand architectural conventions and convert that expertise into scalable technical systems.

What Were Looking For

Strong experience building and deploying machine learning or computer vision systems.Deep understanding of modern computer vision techniques and neural network architectures.Experience with one or more areas such as object detection, segmentation, document AI, multimodal models, vision-language models, image matching, geometry processing, or spatial reasoning.Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch.Experience building datasets, training pipelines, evaluation systems, and production inference workflows.Strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to turn research ideas into maintainable production systems.Comfort working on ambiguous problems where the right technical approach may need to be invented.Ability to move quickly between experimentation, implementation, debugging, and deployment.Excitement about working closely with a small, highly collaborative team in an early-stage environment.

You may be particularly well suited for this role if you have experience with:

Document understanding or document intelligenceCAD, architectural drawings, engineering drawings, maps, diagrams, or other structured visual documentsVector graphics, computational geometry, graph representations, or spatial dataOCR and layout understandingImage registration, feature matching, or correspondenceNumerical optimizationSynthetic data generation and data augmentationFine-tuning or adapting foundation modelsModel evaluation and benchmarking for complex reasoning tasksML infrastructure and large-scale inference systems

Why Geom

Youll have the opportunity to work on AI problems that are both technically difficult and immediately connected to the physical world. Architectural plans contain an enormous amount of structured information, but much of the work required to interpret, modify, and produce them remains manual. Were building the intelligence layer that changes that. At Geom, youll have meaningful ownership from the beginning, work directly with experienced founders and domain experts, and help define a new technical category at the intersection of AI, architecture, and homebuilding.

Don't See a Perfect Match?

Great people rarely fit perfectly into a checklist. If youre excited about computer vision, multimodal AI, geometry, or building intelligent systems that understand the built environment, wed like to hear from you.

Compensation

Pursuant to applicable state and local pay transparency laws, the anticipated salary range for this position is $160,000$220,000 annually. jobs_results.description:
Job Details

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.



Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.





Wanted: Computer Vision (CV) and Machine Learning (ML) Engineer to join the Navigation and Mapping group in the Guidance and Control Section.
  

This unique opportunity is part of the Mechanical Control Systems Division, which is responsible for technology development, advanced concepts, design, development, delivery, integration and test, verification and validation, and operation of complex Mechanical, Thermal, Propulsion, Robotics, and Guidance and Control (G&C) systems.  


As a member of the Navigation and Mapping group, you will investigate, design, and implement advanced capabilities in image-based mapping and navigation. You will use your expertise in CV/ML to design novel solutions to novel problems in map-relative localization, hazard detection/avoidance, illumination invariance, 3D structure recovery, and integration of vision into end-to-end guidance and control solutions for autonomous spacecraft navigation. Ultimately, your work will bridge foundational research and the implementation of mature flight software for JPL missions.  

 

Your work will directly impact the engineering design of JPL’s terrestrial, lunar, Mars-centric and outer planets missions. At the same time, you will continue to advance the state of the art and engage with JPL’s Science community to understand their unique needs and foster collaboration between the engineering and science disciplines. You will be expected to actively seek out opportunities for funding to support your own research agenda in concert with overall Section objectives.  

 

List of Responsibilities: 

Mapping and map-relative navigation for Moonfall, Skyfall, SOLO Collaboration with commercial partners on Artemis/HLS for vision-based solutions to lunar landing Application of ML expertise to partner with scientists on ROSES (Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences) opportunities

Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Physics, Computer Science, related field with a minimum of 6 years of experience, a Master's degree with a minimum of 4 years of experience, or a Ph.D. with a minimum of 2 years related experience.  Extensive understanding and wide application of principles, theories, concepts, and techniques in Machine Learning and Computer Vision Proven ability to adapt theoretical ML models to unique CV problems and develop novel training architectures.  Strong software skills in C++ and Python. Track record of working independently with significant technical latitude to deliver functional capabilities.  
Desired Qualifications: 

Experience with proposal development Publication record in high impact journals and conferences in relevant ML, CV, or aerospace navigation domains.   Background in estimation or control theory.  Experience with participating in multidisciplinary teams.  Strong presentation skills.

jobs_results.description:
QQR LABS


  Principal Engineer, Computer Vision & Edge AI


  Fort Worth, TX / Cincinnati, OH / Austin, TX (full relocation covered) or Remote, US | Full-time


  $220,000 to $280,000 base + 20 to 25% milestone bonus


 Freight fraud and cargo theft drain tens of billions of dollars a year from the US supply chain, and the industry still verifies trucks with paperwork. QQR Labs is building its first product where machine vision meets physical freight. The full scope and excitement of what we are building will be shared during the interview process.


 QQR Labs is the technology arm of QQR Freight, a platform whose sister companies include an asset-based motor carrier and a nationwide 3PL brokerage. We are not a pitch deck. There are trucks, lanes, revenue, and customers behind this, which means a real-world proving ground and a built-in first customer from day one.


 We are hiring the first engineer on the product, and you will own it end to end: the hardware in the field, the models on the edge, and the platform customers log into.


  What you will build


 
  Ruggedized capture hardware: industrial cameras, IR illumination, Jetson-class GPU compute, cellular backhaul, weatherproof enclosures built for unattended outdoor duty
  On-device ML: detection, classification, and OCR on vehicles at highway speed, day and night
  The data platform: high-volume ingestion, entity resolution, search, alerting, APIs
  The data engine: auto-labeling pipelines, continuous retraining, and evaluation loops fed by real-world captures
  Fleet tooling: provisioning, over-the-air updates, and health monitoring for hardware deployed far from a desk
 
 
 Requirements
 

    Who we want


 
  You have shipped computer vision on real hardware in the real world, not just in a notebook. Detection, tracking, OCR, deployed where weather, vibration, and glare live.
  A camera-first mindset: multi-camera perception, vision-only stacks, and models that hold up in rain, glare, and darkness
  Edge and embedded fluency: Linux on ARM, camera pipelines (GStreamer or similar), model optimization (TensorRT, ONNX, quantization)
  Cloud and data competence: Python, AWS or GCP, streaming ingestion, practical MLOps
  You make hardware decisions, work without a playbook, and own outcomes
  If you have built vision systems that live outdoors or on vehicles at scale, you already know this class of problem. Come build one where you hold real skin in the game.
 
 
 Benefits
 

    The package


 
  $220,000 to $280,000 base, plus a 20 to 25% annual bonus tied to build milestones (first unit live in the field, accuracy targets, deployment count)
  Long-term upside beyond salary, covered in the interview process. We want an owner, not an employee.
  Full relocation to Fort Worth, Cincinnati, or Austin, or remote (US) with regular time at HQ and in the field
  Visa sponsorship available, including H-1B transfers
  A funded hardware lab and field deployment budget from day one
  You interview with, and report to, the CEO
